deck: This week highlights shifting financial tides and strategic moves in space.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in a Series C round, focusing on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. With the DoD’s increasing interest in these capabilities, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in a market that's becoming more crowded by the day. This funding comes as the company gears up to meet growing demand from government contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a landscape where cash is king, True Anomaly's ability to attract significant investment suggests that the defense sector is finally taking space security seriously.

stories.head: MDA Space buys Blue Canyon for $620M
stories.body: MDA Space is acquiring Blue Canyon Technologies for $620 million, aiming to strengthen its foothold in the U.S. government market. This deal indicates MDA's ambition to diversify its offerings and enhance its competitiveness in the burgeoning small satellite sector, particularly for defense applications. The acquisition is expected to close by early next year.
stories.soWhat: MDA's move underscores the increasing importance of small satellite capabilities in defense, as the U.S. government looks for innovative solutions to complex challenges.

stories.head: Astrobotic’s sale to Voyager aims for lunar scale-up
stories.body: Astrobotic's planned sale to Voyager is set to accelerate its lunar ambitions, allowing it to meet NASA's demands for lunar landers. The financial details remain under wraps, but the move signals Astrobotic's transition from tech demos to operational missions. This shift is crucial as competition for lunar contracts intensifies.
stories.soWhat: Astrobotic’s pivot could be a bellwether for how quickly companies can adapt to the shifting priorities of government contracts, especially in the lunar domain.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Jio's LEO plans
watchlist.body: Jio Platforms' ambitions for a sovereign LEO constellation could reshape India's satellite internet landscape and challenge existing players.

watchlist.title: Follow developments with Anduril and L3Harris
watchlist.body: Their collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation could signal a new wave of defense partnerships aimed at enhancing space capabilities.

watchlist.title: Watch for Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension indicates strong government reliance on its technology, which might influence future procurement strategies.

watchlist.title: Monitor the hypersonic glide-vehicle tests
watchlist.body: Continued delays in hypersonic testing could impact defense timelines and funding priorities as the U.S. seeks to maintain its technological edge.

talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
